title: C126 — Inline connector reference
introduction:
I start with the face label, then use the cavity drawing to find the matching table row. Read across for circuit identity, wire labels, function and terminal information. Color alone is a shaky address: the male table uses the same color label for different functions, so the circuit identity matters.

The male map includes fuse/circuit-breaker connections and diagnostic network high and low connections. The female map documents a different population, with only the bottom positions outlined white. Read these faces independently. The reason for their unequal population is unexplained here; do not assume every male circuit continues into a populated female cavity. This is a seating chart, and an empty chair is not permission to invent a passenger.

Use the service-parts table to trace shell identifiers to the recorded part entries. This page does not define the gauge convention, Size or Used code legend, or physical viewing direction. It provides no vehicle access, probing, test values or replacement sequence, and it cannot establish circuit health or replacement suitability.

edits.why: I distinguish this drawing by the small rectangular feature on the left and the projecting features on the right. Its top positions are grey, while the middle and bottom positions are outlined white. These are features of the displayed view, not a physical viewing-direction instruction.

Match a printed cavity label to its own row before interpreting the function. The network high and low entries are separate signal identities, not pass/fail readings. The fuse/circuit-breaker entries share a circuit identifier but have different color labels and terminal information; preserve those distinctions rather than smoothing them into one generic connection.

The female illustration has a prominent loop-shaped feature on the right. Its top and middle positions are grey, unlike the male illustration's middle positions. Follow its printed cavity labels and its own table; the common harness label does not make the face records identical.

The populated rows describe fuse/circuit-breaker connections, with wire labels that differ from the male records. The table stops before covering every position drawn, so omitted rows must remain unassigned. NULL in a populated row's Terminal Part Number field leaves that part number unresolved; it does not mean the cavity is empty or authorize borrowing a terminal number from the male table.

Compare Engineering Shell with the selected face's Fpn entry to locate its associated service-part record. Keep the pigtail Gauge entry distinct from the installed circuit's Gauge entry; the table does not explain their relationship or provide a wire-selection rule. Image entries name files rather than displaying the pigtails, and the cross-reference does not teach replacement.
